0|0598e4f08e3da1fea2ee3b4765a44798147a8c62|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"ftrace: Add use of synchronize_rcu_tasks() with dynamic trampolines
The function tracer needs to be more careful than other subsystems when it
comes to freeing data. Especially if that data is actually executable code.
When a single function is traced
column2: a trampoline can be dynamically allocated

column1: which is called to jump to the function trace callback. When the callback is
no longer needed
column2: the dynamic allocated trampoline needs to be freed. This

column1: is where the issues arise. The dynamically allocated trampoline must not be
used again. As function tracing can trace all subsystems
subsystems that are used to serialize aspects of freeing (namely RCU)
must take extra care when doing the freeing.
Before synchronize_rcu_tasks() was around
column2: there was no way for the function

column1: tracer to know that nothing was using the dynamically allocated trampoline
when CONFIG_PREEMPT was enabled. That's because a task could be indefinitely
preempted while sitting on the trampoline. Now with synchronize_rcu_tasks()
it will wait till all tasks have either voluntarily scheduled (not on the
trampoline) or goes into userspace (not on the trampoline). Then it is safe
to free the trampoline even with CONFIG_PREEMPT set.
